title: PACT Authorization Proof
description: Proof-of-human-intent envelope (PACT Specification §17.6) that MAY accompany any PACT message. Carries a cryptographic attestation that a specific HumanPrincipal authorized the action. Attestation-type-specific fields (e.g. `match`, `utterance_hash`, `verifier_id` for `voice-biometric`) are additive — see §18. SCOPE (§17.14, normative): a proof that verifies establishes only that the identified HumanPrincipal authorized THIS EXACT PACT message. It does NOT establish legal identity, role or capacity, authority to bind an entity, intention to sign a particular instrument, satisfaction of witnessing / countersignature / statutory formalities, or enforceability. Silence, TTL expiry, consensus and automated agent votes MUST NOT create or substitute for this envelope (§25.4).

type.description: Attestation type. v2.0 first-class types are `fido2-assertion` and `voice-biometric`; custom types use reverse-domain notation (§18.5).

principal_id.description: The HumanPrincipal that authorized the action — a W3C DID. Verifiers MUST support `did:web` and `did:key`.

credential_id.description: Identifier of the enrolled credential that produced the signature.

challenge_nonce.description: Verifier-issued challenge. Per §17.6, MUST be either (a) signed by the verifier's key (a runtime cryptographic property the JSON Schema cannot encode — assert via `verifier_signed_nonce: true`), OR (b) accompanied by a matching `verifier_id` field in this envelope. Verifiers MUST reject any proof where neither condition holds (§17.7 step 5).

verifier_id.description: Identifier (typically a DID) of the verifier the challenge was issued for. REQUIRED when `verifier_signed_nonce` is not `true` (the schema's `allOf` block at the bottom of this file enforces presence-or-explicit-acknowledgement).

verifier_signed_nonce.description: Annotation: set to `true` if the producer asserts that `challenge_nonce` is itself signed by the verifier's key (the (a) branch of §17.6). Setting this is an assertion to the schema validator, not a cryptographic check — the verifier MUST still validate the signature at §17.7 step 5. When `false` or absent, `verifier_id` MUST be present.

asserted_at.description: When the human authorization was captured (ISO 8601). MUST be within the verifier's allowed clock skew (default ±5 minutes).

signature.description: Base64url-encoded signature over the message payload + `challenge_nonce` + `asserted_at`, per the `type`'s signature suite.

alg.description: Algorithm identifier for this attestation's signature / match. For `fido2-assertion`, MUST be one of the v2.0.2 whitelist below (HMAC / symmetric-key algs are explicitly disallowed — see §17.6). For `voice-biometric`, currently `resemblyzer-v1` (HMAN's #3 PR pins the normative set). Custom attestation types declare their own algs in reverse-domain notation (`com.example.alg-name`).

anyOf.description: voice-biometric reference algorithm (non-normative; HMAN's #3 PR pins the normative set).
Custom attestation alg in reverse-domain notation.

alg_version.description: Version of `alg`. REQUIRED so model swaps / retrains do not silently invalidate enrolled references.

attestation_chain.description: Ordered intermediate attestations for delegated authorization (§17.11). Empty or absent = direct (no delegation). MAX length 3 (direct + 2 sub-delegations) at v2.0. The canonical item shape, the chained-verification algorithm, and trust-decay rules are DEFERRED TO v2.1; v2.0 leaves item structure implementation-defined and v2.0 verifiers that cannot themselves verify a non-empty chain MUST reject the proof as `unverifiable` (§17.11). Implementations that do not support delegation MUST reject any proof where this array is non-empty.

match.description: Speaker-verification result. Present for `voice-biometric` and reused by future biometric modalities (§18.3). Full normative shape lands via HMAN's #3 PR.

utterance_hash.description: Base64url hash of the spoken utterance, binding a `voice-biometric` assertion to what was said (§18.3, normative).

payload_hash.description: v2.3 (§17.6, §25.7 check 4). Base64url SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON encoding of the exact payload being authorized. REQUIRED whenever this proof is presented to release a §25.6 apply guard (i.e. whenever `effect_class` is present). The `signature` MUST commit to it. A verifier MUST refuse an attestation whose `payload_hash` does not equal the hash it computes over the payload actually being applied — including an earlier revision of the same proposal.

scope.description: v2.3 (§17.6, §25.7 check 5). The specific effect this attestation authorizes, in reverse-domain or path form — e.g. `pact.apply.transaction:txn_9f2`, `pact.apply.document:doc_abc/sec:intro`. REQUIRED for a guarded apply. A proof MUST NOT release a guard for an effect outside its scope.

effect_class.description: v2.3 (§25.5). The effect class the human was shown when they attested. REQUIRED for a guarded apply. A proof carrying `internal-reversible` MUST NOT release a guard on an `external-irreversible` apply (§25.7 check 5).

allOf.description: §17.6 verifier-binding rule: challenge_nonce MUST be either verifier-signed (asserted via verifier_signed_nonce: true) OR accompanied by verifier_id.

v2.3 §25.7 guarded-apply binding: a proof that declares an `effect_class` is being presented to release a §25.6 apply guard, and MUST therefore also carry `payload_hash` (check 4) and `scope` (check 5). Schema-validity is necessary but not sufficient — the verifier MUST additionally recompute the payload hash and evaluate scope coverage at runtime.
v2.3 §25.7: `payload_hash` and `scope` are only meaningful together with the effect class the human was shown. Presenting either without `effect_class` is an incomplete guarded-apply binding.
